domain: Islamic Jurisprudence / Legal Theory / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: The four Sunni schools of jurisprudence (madhahib) — Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali — represent competing readings of the shared jurisprudential-method kernel that have coexisted for over a millennium without one displacing the others. Each school grounds interpretive authority differently while accepting the same foundational texts (Quran, Sunnah), creating a legitimated plurality within Sunni Islam where a Muslim may lawfully follow any of the four schools.

key_entities: Hanafi School (Abu Hanifa, d. 767 CE; emphasizes qiyas/analogical reasoning, ra'y/juridical opinion)
Maliki School (Malik ibn Anas, d. 795 CE; emphasizes Medinan practice, maslaha/public interest)
Shafi'i School (al-Shafi'i, d. 820 CE; systematizer; strict hadith hierarchy, rejects istihsan)
Hanbali School (Ahmad ibn Hanbal, d. 855 CE; textualist; minimizes qiyas, rejects ra'y)
Shared Kernel: usul al-fiqh (jurisprudential methodology for deriving rulings from sources)
Authority Structures: madhhab taqlid (school adherence), mujtahid (qualified interpreter), mufti (jurisconsult)
Ottoman Empire (institutionalized Hanafi as state law)
Modern Reform Movements (Salafism, direct-source advocacy, madhhab rejection)
key_tensions: Strict hadith hierarchy (Shafi'i) vs contextualized practice (Maliki)
School loyalty (taqlid) vs direct-source interpretation (salafi critique)
Legal diversity (madhhab plurality) vs standardization pressure (modern nation-states)

axes.structural_delta: Jurisprudential authority grounded in systematic analogical reasoning (qiyas) and juridical opinion (ra'y); permits istihsan (juristic preference) when strict analogy produces hardship; generates permissive rulings in commercial/contract domains
axes.primary_observable: Frequency of qiyas invocation in fatawa; use of istihsan; commercial contract diversity under Hanafi vs other schools
axes.selection_reason: Most structurally permissive reading; grounds authority in rationalist method; highest commercial-law extractiveness differential

axes.structural_delta: Jurisprudential authority grounded in strict textual adherence; minimizes qiyas, rejects ra'y and istihsan; treats prophetic hadith as dispositive even if weak; generates restrictive rulings in worship/practice domains
axes.primary_observable: Hadith citation density in fatawa; rejection rate of qiyas-based rulings; worship practice restrictiveness
axes.beneficiary: hadith scholars, purist communities, anti-innovation factions
axes.selection_reason: Polar opposite to Hanafi on authority-grounding axis; textualist vs rationalist; structurally distinct beneficiary/victim sets

axes.structural_delta: Jurisprudential authority grounded in explicit source hierarchy: Quran > authentic Sunnah > ijma' (consensus) > qiyas (restricted); rejects istihsan and local custom (urf); generates methodologically strict but substantively moderate rulings
axes.primary_observable: Adherence to four-source hierarchy in fatawa; rejection of urf-based rulings; hadith authentication standards
axes.beneficiary: hadith scholars, systematizers, scholars claiming methodological purity
axes.victim: localist jurists relying on urf (reading foreclosed)
axes.selection_reason: Methodological systematizer; distinct from Hanafi (rejects istihsan) and Hanbali (uses qiyas); grounds authority in explicit hierarchy rather than textualism or rationalism alone

axes.structural_delta: Jurisprudential authority grounded in continuous Medinan communal practice ('amal ahl al-Madina) as living Sunnah; prioritizes maslaha (public interest); treats transmitted practice as superior to isolated hadith reports; generates context-sensitive rulings
axes.primary_observable: Citation of Medinan practice vs hadith; maslaha invocation frequency; context-dependency of rulings
axes.beneficiary: regional scholars, administrators balancing law and custom, maslaha advocates
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: structurally similar to Hanafi (pragmatic, context-sensitive) but less extreme; selecting three polar readings (Hanafi rationalist, Hanbali textualist, Shafi'i systematizer) captures the authority-grounding topology

axes.primary_observable: Frequency of school-switching; legal regime recognition of multi-madhhab courts; persistence of school affiliation across generations
axes.beneficiary: madhahib institutions, scholars claiming madhhab authority
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: downstream coordination mechanism, not a reading of the kernel itself; omega material on how plurality is sustained institutionally

axes.human_readable: Modern Standardization Pressure (Nation-State vs Madhhab Plurality)

axes.primary_observable: Codification rate of Islamic law; salafi movement growth; state attempts to unify madhhab jurisdiction
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: modern external pressure on the system, not a reading of the kernel; omega material on system fragility

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Jurisprudential authority grounded in Medinan communal practice and maslaha
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Structurally similar to Hanafi (pragmatic, context-sensitive); selecting three polar readings (rationalist, textualist, systematizer) captures authority-grounding topology without redundancy

omegas.description: How does the taqlid institution sustain four contradictory readings for 1200+ years without one displacing the others? Is this a Rope (successful coordination) or evidence that the readings coexist_with rather than foreclose despite axiom contradictions?
omegas.source: Deferred axis taqlid_institution + axiom contradiction observation

omegas.description: Modern standardization pressure (nation-state codification, salafi anti-taqlid movements) may collapse the licensed plurality. Is this a Snare extracting from the madhhab system, or a Mountain of state sovereignty that the commitment system cannot resist?

Is the usul al-fiqh kernel genuinely ambiguous (permitting four legitimate readings), or is the plurality a historical accident sustained by institutional inertia? If the former, the kernel itself may be a Scaffold; if the latter, a fossilized Rope.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) — no analysis of whether the kernel's ambiguity is structural or contingent

omegas.description: The three selected readings ground authority in rationalism (Hanafi), textualism (Hanbali), and hierarchy (Shafi'i). Maliki grounds it in transmitted practice. Does practice-authority constitute a fourth distinct pole, or is it captured by rationalism + context sensitivity?

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Topic is archetypal commitment system with contested kernel. Four readings identified; three selected to capture authority-grounding topology (rationalist, textualist, systematizer). Maliki deferred as structurally intermediate. Taqlid and modern pressure deferred as downstream/external to kernel itself.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Usul al-fiqh: the shared jurisprudential methodology for deriving Islamic legal rulings from foundational sources (Quran, Sunnah, ijma', qiyas). All four schools accept these sources; they differ on which sources take priority, how to weight them, and what additional methods (ra'y, istihsan, maslaha, urf) are legitimate.
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Each school grounds interpretive legitimacy differently: Hanafi in rationalist qiyas, Maliki in Medinan transmitted practice, Shafi'i in explicit source hierarchy, Hanbali in strict textual adherence. Taqlid institution legitimates all four by requiring laypeople to follow one school consistently.

axiom_contradictions.basis: Hanafi's axiom that juridical reasoning (ra'y) is a legitimate source of law is mutually exclusive with Hanbali's axiom that human reasoning beyond strict textualism is illegitimate innovation. No single coherent framework can hold both.

Shafi'i's axiom that authenticated hadith always supersedes local custom (urf) is mutually exclusive with Maliki's axiom that continuous Medinan practice supersedes isolated hadith reports. No single coherent framework can hold both.

Hanafi's axiom that istihsan (juristic preference overriding strict analogy) is legitimate is mutually exclusive with Shafi'i's axiom that only the four explicit sources (Quran, Sunnah, ijma', restricted qiyas) are legitimate. No single coherent framework can hold both.
